reasoning_summary: The bug diff deletes the entire distance method of OptimalStringAlignment, leaving the class body as pass, so the public capability is absent rather than miscomputed. The reference repair reinstates the whole method. ALGORITHM is plausible because the restored body is a dynamic-programming routine, but this is a wholesale capability loss rather than an ordinary local implementation mistake, so rule 7 selects FUNCTION.

The bug diff strips the whole embed_font branch from to_svg, which is an optional but self-contained SVG export capability, together with the font_style derivation it depends on. The reference repair reinstates both blocks unchanged. The missing font_style assignment alone would suggest ASSIGNMENT under rule 4, but the bulk of the correction restores an absent feature rather than a single value, so rule 7 selects FUNCTION.

The bug diff weakens the skip condition in attr_attributes_transform from "elif not use_bare_annotations: continue" to an unconditional "else: continue", so bare annotated class attributes are always discarded, matching the specification and the failing attrs annotation test. The reference repair restores that condition along with the NEW_ATTRS_NAMES set and the use_bare_annotations predicate it reads. The deleted definitions make ASSIGNMENT plausible under rule 4, but they exist only to feed the guard, and the operative correction is the branch condition, so rule 5 selects CHECKING.

The bug diff makes fetch_data_files swallow per-file download exceptions into warn_and_log, dropping the error accumulator and the "if error: raise RuntimeError(...)" post-condition. The reference repair restores exactly that accumulation and terminal check, and the specification and failing download-failure test both describe the missing RuntimeError. The correction is checking logic over the outcome of the downloads.

The bug diff replaces the hash-combination scheme in combine_hashes_lists: it sorts the outer item list instead of sorting within each item, drops the "--" element separator and the bytes encoding, folds the prefix into the hashed input, and returns the bare digest instead of prefix + digest. The reference repair restores the original computation. Both failing tests compare against fixed expected digests and the specification reports inconsistent hash output, so the correction is a local implementation fix to the computation itself.

The bug diff drops the SyntaxRule base class from _ArglistRule, so a class still registered through ErrorFinder.register_rule no longer inherits the rule contract the normalizer framework instantiates and calls. The reference repair restores the base class alone. The breakage is conformance to a component boundary rather than any computation inside the class, and its breadth is visible in the 122 failing tests including collection of parso itself.

The bug diff rewrites the expansion body of _get_from_environ with an ad-hoc {{...}} regex that drops the _EXPANDED_VAR_PATTERN match, the ":-default" substitution and recursion-guard on default, the search-based general expansion path, and the escaped "\$" unescaping. The reference repair restores that procedure within the same method and signature, and the three failing tests cover exactly the full-expand, default-expand and escaped-expand paths the specification names. The correction is a local implementation fix, not a design change.

The bug diff rewrites HTTP1Connection.finish and loses the branch that sets _disconnect_on_finish when the response finishes while _read_finished is still false, along with stream.set_nodelay. The reference repair restores that sequencing. The observable defect in the specification and in the early-return and client-close tests is a client that hangs indefinitely because connection teardown is never ordered against the still-incomplete body read, which is coordination over a shared connection rather than a wrong computation; the restored flag also makes ASSIGNMENT arguable, so rule 2 decides.

The bug diff drops "bin_op = aug_opnode.op.strip('=')" from _get_aug_flow and reuses the augmented operator for the plain binary fallbacks, so _bin_op receives "+=" where "+" is required. The four type-relationship branches keep their original method ordering, so this derived value is the only semantic change, and the reference repair restores exactly that initialization and its use. The correction is a missing local value derivation, matching the augmented-assignment inference failures in the tests and specification.

The bug diff removes "if self._selects: self._select_into = True" from QueryBuilder.into, so the flag that makes the builder emit SELECT ... INTO is never set; the reference repair restores it. All three failing tests are SelectIntoTests and the specification names the unset _select_into flag directly. The same edit also drops the AttributeError guard on a repeated into call, which makes CHECKING plausible, but that guard is not what the failing tests exercise, so rule 4 selects ASSIGNMENT.

The bug diff narrows the route dispatch test in get_endpoints from "isinstance(route, (Mount, Host))" to Mount only, dropping the Host import and the empty path-prefix branch, so Host sub-routes are silently skipped during schema generation as the specification and the failing schema tests describe. The reference repair widens the test back and restores the branch. The restored "path = ''" assignment makes ASSIGNMENT arguable, but it is unreachable until the type test admits Host, so rule 5 selects CHECKING.

The bug diff hoists "self.change_time = change_time" in _NodeCacheItem.__init__ above the "if change_time is None: change_time = time.time()" default, so the attribute is stored as None while self.last_used still receives the substituted timestamp. The reference repair moves the assignment back below the default. The correction is a single attribute initialized with the wrong value, which is what the cache timestamp tests exercise.

The bug diff deletes the Group NamedTuple, stores groups as bare dicts, and removes the describe_group operation from both the backend model and the response handler, so the DescribeGroup action no longer exists and list_groups serialization breaks where responses.py still calls g._asdict(). The reference repair reinstates the type and both halves of the operation. The models-to-responses contract breakage makes INTERFACE plausible, but that is downstream of removing a whole capability and its data abstraction across two modules, so rule 7 selects FUNCTION.

The bug diff inverts or narrows a cluster of predicates in cli.py: the except clause drops from OSError to FileNotFoundError, "if v is not None" becomes "is None", "if success" becomes "if not success", "if not commandline" becomes "if commandline", and the run override filter is negated, with the exit codes flipped alongside. The reference repair restores each condition. The sorted-to-reversed swap and the "not quote" argument make ALGORITHM and INTERFACE arguable for individual lines, but the corrections are dominantly guard and condition logic, so rule 5 selects CHECKING.

The bug diff deletes the "for plugin in self.plugins: plugin.init_spec(self)" loop from APISpec.__init__, so registered plugins are never handed the spec through their init_spec hook; the surrounding version-range check is only restated equivalently and self.plugins is still assigned. The reference repair restores that loop. The defect is the missing invocation of the plugin registration hook across the spec-to-plugin boundary, which the failing test_components_can_be_accessed_by_plugin_in_init_spec names directly. Reading the loop as a missing initialization would suggest ASSIGNMENT, so rule 3 decides.

The bug diff moves "expr_stmt = containing_leaf.search_ancestor('expr_stmt')" in BackslashNode.__init__ below the "if expr_stmt is not None" branch that reads it, so the local is used before it is bound, and relocates self.parent to the top. The reference repair puts the binding back ahead of its use. The correction is the placement of a local initialization relative to its consumer, which the PEP 8 normalizer tests over backslash continuations exercise.

The bug diff makes get_var_names compile the regex and hand a re.Pattern object to Series.str.match, and correspondingly weakens that API's "pat: str" annotation and docstring in the strings accessor. The pyarrow-backed match implementation only accepts a string pattern, so the call raises "expected string or bytes-like object, got 're.Pattern'" as the specification reports. The reference repair passes the regex string again and restores the declared parameter type. The correction is the argument contract between the reshape module and the string accessor API.

The bug diff deletes the input normalization "string = string.replace('\\', '/')" from matches and swaps re.match for re.search. Both failing cases are backslash paths, so the missing normalization assignment is the operative loss, and the reference repair restores it together with anchored matching. Rule 1 was considered because the function lives in build_helpers, but the correction is to path-matching logic rather than to build or package state; the re.search swap makes ALGORITHM plausible, so rule 4 selects ASSIGNMENT.

The bug diff rewrites decorated_main so that _run_hydra is called without the args_parser argument the working code passes, and reads args.config_file in place of args.experimental_rerun. Both are contract mismatches at a call boundary rather than wrong computations inside the function, which fits the breadth of the failure across 105 tests that exercise ordinary runs. The reference repair restores the argument and the original attribute.

The bug diff deletes the "-f/--force" subparser argument from remote_add and replaces "remotes.add(r, force=args.force, index=args.index)" with a bare add followed by a separate move call; the only change in remotes.py is a trailing newline, so the duplicate-URL checking code itself is untouched and merely never receives force. The reference repair restores the option and the parameterized call. The defect is the command-line surface exposed to the user and the arguments crossing from the CLI into the remotes API, matching the duplicate-name, duplicate-url and insert tests.

The bug diff changes the Maintainability Index formula in mi_compute: the comments term becomes sin(sqrt(2.4 * comments / 100)) instead of sin(sqrt(2.46 * radians(comments))), and the final "nn_mi * 100 / 171.0" normalization is dropped in favour of a bare clamp. The reference repair restores the original expression. Both failing tests assert exact MI values and the specification names the comments scaling factor, so the correction is to the computation itself within one function.

The bug diff touches only test.py, replacing the body of test_parse_time with a different set of inputs and stricter expectations, including an assertRaises(ValueError) and exact SimpleTZ results that the unchanged parse_time does not satisfy; no library module is modified and the sole failing test is the rewritten method itself. The reference repair restores the original timestamp list and its "is not None" assertions, so the correction is to assertion and expected-value logic. Rule 5 selects CHECKING over reading the changed expected values as ASSIGNMENT; confidence is low because the defective artifact is the test rather than the library behaviour the specification describes.

The bug diff permutes the body of ThaiLocale._format_relative so that "return relative_string" is the first statement, before relative_string is bound from direction.format(humanized), leaving the "now" early return and the seconds space-stripping unreachable behind it. The reference repair restores the original order. The operative correction is that the value must be assigned before it is returned, which the three Thai relative-format tests exercise; reading the whole permuted body as control flow makes ALGORITHM plausible, so rule 4 decides.

The bug diff moves "direct_url = self.direct_url" in editable_project_location to the end of the property, below the "if direct_url and direct_url.is_local_editable()" branch that reads it, so the name is unbound at its first use. The reference repair restores the binding to the top. The correction is the placement of one local initialization relative to its consumer; the surrounding egg-link and url_to_path logic is otherwise unchanged.

The bug diff weakens the guard in websocket_receive from "message.get('text') is not None" to a bare "'text' in message" in both WebsocketConsumer and AsyncWebsocketConsumer, so a message carrying text=None takes the text branch instead of falling through to bytes. The reference repair restores the None test in both places. The correction is purely the validation condition on the value before use, matching the specification and the none-text test.

The bug diff replaces the bounds check in millfn, which raised NumOutOfRangeError for "ind > len(mill) - 1", with a silent clamp that returns mill[-1] for any out-of-range index. The reference repair restores the range check and the exception. The correction is validation of an index before use, which is exactly what the specification and test_millfn describe; the incidentally dropped "ind: int = 0" default is secondary.

The bug diff deletes "y = (longitude_1 - longitude_2) * coef" from geo.distance while the very next statement still computes sqrt(x * x + y * y), leaving y unbound. The reference repair restores that single line. The correction is one missing value assignment, and the breadth of the 30 failing tests follows from every distance-dependent computation in the module going through this function.

The bug diff reorders get_route_path so that the "if not path.startswith(root_path)" test comes first, ahead of "path = scope['path']" and "root_path = scope.get('root_path', '')", leaving both names unbound at their first use. The reference repair restores the bindings to the top of the function ahead of every guard. The correction is the placement of the two local initializations, and the 322 failing tests follow from every routed request passing through this helper.

The bug diff removes describe_account_assignment_creation_status and describe_account_assignment_deletion_status from both the backend model and the response handler, drops the deleted_account_assignments store and the removal bookkeeping in delete_account_assignment, and strips include_request_id from AccountAssignment.to_json, substituting a freshly generated uuid in responses.py. The reference repair reinstates all of it. The lost RequestId field makes INTERFACE arguable, but two complete API operations and their backing state are absent, so rule 7 selects FUNCTION.

The bug diff removes two assignments from parse_implicit_response: the binding "fragment = urlparse.urlparse(uri).fragment", which the very next parse_qsl call consumes, and the "params[key] = int(params[key])" cast that turns expires_in into an integer, replaced by a bare pass. The reference repair restores both. The correction is missing value assignments, which is what the implicit-response and token-response parsing tests check.

The bug diff collapses the parsed pairs into an OrderedDict before interpolation and then feeds values.items() to resolve_variables, whereas the working code passes the raw parse() sequence. Deduplicating first discards the repeated "c" entry and its file position, so a later redefinition can no longer resolve against a variable defined after the earlier one, which is exactly the a/c/d/c case in the specification and the single failing test. The reference repair passes the raw values again. The changed "if self._dict" guard makes CHECKING arguable, but the defect is the data structure handed to the resolution step, so rule 6 selects ALGORITHM.

The bug diff weakens both validations in parse_address: the exactly-one-colon test "len(words) != 2" becomes a mere "':' not in address" with an rsplit, and the port range test "not 0 < port < 2**16" becomes "port < 0 or port > 65535", which admits port zero. The two failing tests are precisely the port-zero and too-many-colons cases, and the reference repair restores both conditions. The correction is validation logic on the input.

The bug diff passes a bare "jobs" to self._sync_import where the working code reads kwargs.get("jobs"), so the argument refers to a name the method never binds, and it also deletes the "if no_download: self.ignore_outs()" branch. The reference repair restores both. The operative correction is supplying the argument its value from kwargs, an internal call rather than a component boundary; the removed no_download branch makes CHECKING arguable, so rule 4 selects ASSIGNMENT.

The bug diff deletes inspect and inspect_err from both Ok and Err, so the side-effect inspection feature of the Result type does not exist at all and calls raise AttributeError as the specification shows. The reference repair reinstates all four methods with their original bodies. Because the absent code is public API surface, INTERFACE is arguable, but nothing is mismatched or miscomputed and an entire documented capability is missing, so rule 7 selects FUNCTION.

The bug diff swaps the scale values between two branches of the epoch-extraction logic, giving EPOCH_NANOSECOND a scale of None and the fallback else branch 10**9. The branch conditions themselves are untouched, and the reference repair swaps the two assignments back. The correction is the value bound in each branch, which the Snowflake timestamp test exercises.

The bug diff drops "or local == '_ignore_'" from the skip condition in infer_enum_class, so _ignore_ is inferred as an ordinary member, and separately removes the _value_ and _name_ property definitions from the synthesized member template. The reference repair restores both. The missing sunder properties make FUNCTION arguable for that half, but the correction includes guard logic that selects which locals are processed, and rule 5 precedes rule 7 in the frozen order.

The bug diff replaces the whole body of the "_VALIDATORS" loop in find_validators with pass, so the registry is walked but never consulted and every type falls through to the arbitrary-types branch or the "no validator found" RuntimeError. The reference repair restores the issubclass match, the IfConfig handling, the yields and the TypeError translation. Because the restored code contains type tests, CHECKING is arguable, but what is missing is the whole lookup and dispatch procedure inside one function rather than a single guard, so rule 6 selects ALGORITHM.

The bug diff swaps the two branch bodies in _extract_metrics while leaving the "if m not in (None, {})" test unchanged, so a successfully parsed metric is logged as unsupported and never stored, and only empty results are written into ret. The reference repair puts "ret[key] = m" back on the true branch. The correction is the placement of the accumulating assignment, not the condition, and every metrics show test depends on it.

The bug diff corrupts the byte-level decoding throughout decode.py: songpos and pitchwheel reverse which data byte is shifted and add an off-by-one to MIN_PITCHWHEEL, the channel nibble becomes "status_byte | 0xf0" and later ">> 4", and the payload slice becomes msg_bytes[:-1] instead of [1:]. The reference repair restores each expression. Rule 5 was considered because the sysex end test and the "if check" flag are also inverted, and rule 4 because each wrong expression sits in an assignment, but the defect is systematically wrong bit manipulation across the decode procedure, so rule 6 selects ALGORITHM.

The bug diff removes two entries from the tool-to-distribution mapping initialized in _SystemPackageManagerTool: "nobara" from the dnf list and "endeavouros" from the pacman list. The reference repair adds them back; no lookup or matching logic is touched. Rule 1 was considered because the subject matter is package managers, but the defect is in this product's own data table rather than in build, version or packaging state of the software under review, so rule 4 selects ASSIGNMENT for the missing initialized values.

The bug diff replaces the scan over source_patches that matched each slice by equality with a dictionary keyed on slice objects, and the patch lookup no longer resolves, so every slice falls through to the raw source and patches are never applied. The reference repair restores the equality scan with its for/else fallback. The specification names the lookup mechanism, and the correction changes the local data structure used to match patches to slices, which is ALGORITHM under rule 6; confidence is medium because the packet shows the changed lookup but not the runtime mechanism by which it fails to match.

The bug diff removes three assignments from describe_node: the class-suffix append becomes a bare pass, the "uid = uids.get(node)" binding is deleted so uid is unbound at the "if uid is None" test, and the "{%02d}" suffix append is dropped. The reference repair restores all three. The surrounding conditions are untouched, so the correction is missing value assignments within one function.

The bug diff moves "self._cv.notify_all()" in BufferedPipe.close to after "self._event.set()", changing the order in which waiters on the condition variable and waiters on the event are released while the lock is held. The reference repair moves the notify_all back ahead of the event set. The correction is purely the ordering of a synchronization notification, which the specification also describes as a race in the notification mechanism.

The bug diff rewrites tokenFeatures with an entirely different feature computation: the token_clean and token_abbrev normalization regexes are gone, and the original keys such as abbrev, word, trailing.zeros, length, directional and street_name are replaced by a different token.* set derived from the raw token. The reference repair restores the original derivation. Because the emitted feature names are what the downstream tagger consumes, INTERFACE is arguable, and the total loss of parsing makes FUNCTION arguable, but the packet shows one function's computation being replaced in place, so rule 6 selects ALGORITHM.

The bug diff rewrites the package's component inventory: several hundred entries are dropped from the generated LEXERS registry in _mapping.py, the pygments/lexers/lean.py module is deleted, and a superseded LeanLexer is reinstated inside theorem.py, whose imports do not include "include", so importing it raises the NameError the specification reports and 5060 tests fail at collection. The reference repair restores the registry entries and the lean module and removes the resurrected class. The scale of the loss makes FUNCTION arguable, but the correction is to which modules the package ships and how they are registered, so rule 1 selects BUILD_PACKAGE_MERGE.

The bug diff removes the GetAdministratorAccount operation across all three layers: the admin_accounts store and get_administrator_account method in models.py, the response handler in responses.py, and the "/detector/<id>/administrator" route in urls.py. Nothing is left mismatched; the capability simply does not exist, which is what the specification and both failing tests report. The deleted route is API surface, which makes INTERFACE arguable, but a whole operation is absent rather than miswired, so rule 7 selects FUNCTION.

The bug diff rewrites get_expected_length and drops the final YBR_FULL_422 adjustment "length = length // 3 * 2", so the subsampled packing of that photometric interpretation is no longer accounted for; it also replaces get_nr_frames with inline frame handling. Every failing test is a test_length_ybr_422 parameterization, and the reference repair restores the adjustment. Because the missing step is a conditional assignment, CHECKING and ASSIGNMENT are arguable, but what is absent is a term of the length calculation itself, so rule 6 selects ALGORITHM.

The bug diff deletes from seed_instance the first-call creation of a per-instance random_module.Random and the "self._is_seeded = True" flag, so the generator keeps seeding the shared module-level random and every instance ends up on the same state, as the specification describes. The reference repair restores both. The deleted block is introduced by an "if self.__random == random" test, which makes CHECKING arguable, but the guard exists only to perform the initialization, so rule 4 selects ASSIGNMENT.

The bug diff drops the Import base class from ImportFrom, so the node class no longer inherits the Import and PythonBaseNode contract that the parser and normalizers rely on when handling import_from nodes. The reference repair restores the base class and nothing else. The defect is conformance to a class contract rather than any computation in the body, and the failing tests span parsing, diff-parsing and normalizer checks that all traverse import nodes.

The bug diff removes the pkglist capability from the export command: the MultiPackagesList and PackagesList import, the construction of the exported package list, the dict return carrying both pkglist and reference, and the registered "pkglist" formatter, with json_export narrowed to take a bare ref. The reference repair restores all of it. Because the command return value and its formatters were changed in lockstep there is no residual contract mismatch, so INTERFACE is arguable but secondary; an output capability of the command is simply gone, and rule 7 selects FUNCTION.

The bug diff changes the slice bound in extract_shortcodes from "data[i:j + 1]" to "data[i:j - 1]", so the captured shortcode chunk stops two tokens short of its SHORTCODE_END and the stored body is truncated; the surrounding loop, condition and return are unchanged. The reference repair restores the bound. Because the wrong expression sits in an assignment, ASSIGNMENT is arguable, but the defect is a boundary computation in the extraction logic, so rule 6 selects ALGORITHM.

The bug diff replaces the body of _decode_data_sequence, which read the Basic Offset Table and each fragment through _read_item inside a DicomBytesIO context, with a hand-rolled tag and length walk over the stream. The hand-rolled walk loses the item framing the helper provides and ends up on a misaligned tag, producing the "Unexpected tag ... fragment items" ValueError the specification quotes. The reference repair restores the _read_item loop. The raise comes from a tag test, which makes CHECKING arguable, but the condition only fires because the parsing procedure itself is wrong, so rule 6 selects ALGORITHM.

The bug diff repoints backends.py at "from dask.compatibility import entry_points" in place of "from dask._compatibility import importlib_metadata", so the module fails to import at all with the ImportError the specification quotes and nothing in the file is reachable. It also reorders CreationDispatch.__init__ so entrypoint_class follows name and becomes optional. The reference repair restores the import and the signature. Rule 1 was considered because a missing module can look like a version mismatch, but no packaged component changed; the defect is this module's dependency and call contracts, so rule 3 selects INTERFACE.

The bug diff deletes classify, provide_overview_context_and_uptodate and get_other_language_variants from ClassifyAuthors, which the code context shows is a nikola.plugin_categories.Taxonomy subclass; those methods are the overrides the taxonomy machinery calls, so the plugin no longer satisfies the protocol its host invokes. The reference repair reinstates all three. Reading the loss as a missing author-pages capability supports FUNCTION, but the removed members are the plugin's side of a component contract, so rule 3 selects INTERFACE.

The bug diff removes the "num1 = float(num1)" coercion from _get_numbers_distance while leaving the identical coercion for num2 in place, so the first operand keeps its original numeric type through the subsequent division. The reference repair restores it. The correction is a missing value conversion assigned back to the operand, not a change to any condition, and the two failing cases are the numeric distance comparisons that depend on it.

The bug diff stops removing "label_size" from kwargs in plot_resources, so an attribute the Bokeh figure does not accept is forwarded and raises the AttributeError quoted in the specification, and it also writes f.plot_height where the current API exposes f.height. The reference repair restores the pop and the height attribute along with the version warnings. Rule 1 was considered because the surrounding code branches on BOKEH_VERSION, but nothing about this package's build or dependency state changed; the correction is what this module passes to and reads from an external library's API, so rule 3 selects INTERFACE.

The bug diff rewrites Plane._getrange to yield integer grid indices computed from "(x0 - self.x0) // gridsize" instead of the grid coordinates that drange produced, so the keys it emits no longer address the buckets the plane stores objects under, and it also drops the early return for boxes disjoint from the plane. The reference repair restores the drange enumeration and the guard. The removed early return makes CHECKING arguable, but the defect is the key space of a spatial index enumeration, so rule 6 selects ALGORITHM.

The bug diff moves Literal from the typing import list to typing_extensions and drops the ParamSpec import, so type_adapter.py resolves those names against different modules than the rest of the package; it also removes the module-level P and TypeAdapterT definitions and relocates a _frame_depth decorator. The reference repair restores the original import sources and definitions. The specification attributes the failure to where Literal is imported from, and the dropped module-level bindings make ASSIGNMENT arguable, so rule 3 selects INTERFACE for the module dependency contract.

The bug diff swaps the bodies of the "elif not segment.segments" and "else" branches in _iter_templated_patches, leaving both conditions untouched: childless raw segments now run the deep traversal while segments that do have children hit the early return. The reference repair puts each body back on its own branch. Since the effect is that the abort fires under the wrong condition, CHECKING is arguable, but no condition was altered and the correction restores the recursion's control flow, so rule 6 selects ALGORITHM.

The bug diff narrows Path.__eq__ to an "if not isinstance(other, Path): return False" gate, dropping the "elif type(other) is TType" case that compared self.path_t.__ops__ against other.__ops__, so a Path never equals an equivalent TType. The reference repair restores that branch. Reading __eq__ as comparison logic makes ALGORITHM arguable, but the correction is the type test that decides which operands are accepted and how they are compared, so rule 5 selects CHECKING.

The bug diff deletes two bindings from Generator.expressions: the "expressions" local derived from expression.args or sqls, which the immediately following "if not expressions" reads, and the per-item "comments" local that the result f-strings interpolate. Both names are then unbound at their uses. The reference repair restores the two assignments and nothing else.

The bug diff replaces three "- 1" offsets with "- 0" in the tokenizer's delimited-text scan: the advance past a multi-character delimiter, the start index recorded before advancing, and the end bound of the slice appended to text. The reference repair restores each offset. Because one of them sits in an assignment, ASSIGNMENT is arguable, but the defect is index arithmetic in the scanning loop, so rule 6 selects ALGORITHM.

The bug diff swaps the two bodies of the "if py311_or_above" branch, leaving the condition intact: on 3.11 and above frame_summary is now rebuilt without the end_lineno, colno and end_colno adjustments, while the enhanced construction is assigned on the older-Python path. The reference repair returns each construction to its own branch. Rule 1 was considered because the branch keys off an interpreter version, but no build or packaging state is involved; each branch assigns frame_summary the wrong value, so rule 4 selects ASSIGNMENT.

The bug diff moves "off = self.off" in the CT_Transform2D.y getter below the "if off is None" test that reads it, leaving the name unbound at its first use. The reference repair puts the binding back above the guard. The correction is the placement of one local initialization; the breadth of the failing shape and connector tests follows from every position read going through this property.

The bug diff rewrites the exported UID surface of uid.py: HTJ2K, JPEG XL and the MPEG frame-level constants are deleted, JPEGLossless is renamed JPEGLosslessP14, and a deprecating __getattr__ shim is added, while the gdcm and pylibjpeg handlers are repointed at the renamed name. Names still referenced elsewhere are then undefined, giving the import-time NameError on HTJ2KLossless that the specification reports. The reference repair restores the constants and the handler references. Rule 1 was considered since the shim reads as an older API generation, but no packaged file or build input changed; the defect is the module's exported names and the dependents that import them, so rule 3 selects INTERFACE.

The bug diff hoists "return [k for k, c in seen_keys.items() if c > 1]" to the first line of Request.duplicate_params and pushes the "seen_keys = collections.defaultdict(int)" initialization below it, so the name is unbound when the return evaluates it and the counting loop is unreachable. The reference repair restores the original order. Treating the permuted body as control flow makes ALGORITHM arguable, but the operative correction is binding the accumulator before it is read, so rule 4 selects ASSIGNMENT.

The bug diff replaces StyleGuide.excluded's local helper, which ran expand_paths over a path and tested both the bare filename and the parent-joined path, with a single delegation to self._file_checker_manager.is_path_excluded on the joined path only. The bare filename is then never tested on its own, which is the parent-handling failure the specification describes. The reference repair restores the helper and the two-way disjunction. Delegating to another component's method makes INTERFACE arguable, but the correction restores this method's own exclusion logic, so rule 6 selects ALGORITHM.

The bug diff removes the --test-missing feature of conan create in full: the -tm subparser argument, the BINARY_BUILD import, the incompatibility check against --test-folder="", and the branch that clears test_conanfile_path when the root binary was not built from source. The reference repair restores all four. Rule 3 was considered because the flag is user-facing CLI surface and rule 5 because the deleted skip logic and the raised ConanException are conditions, but nothing is left mismatched and an entire documented option and its effect are gone, so rule 7 selects FUNCTION.

The bug diff rewrites WSGIHeaderDict.__getitem__ to fetch through self.raw and return value.decode('latin1') for bytes, dropping the "encode('latin1').decode('utf8')" round trip that recovers UTF-8 header text from the WSGI latin-1 representation, which produces the mojibake the specification shows. The reference repair restores the original body. Reading the lost step as an inappropriate value conversion supports ASSIGNMENT, but the whole lookup and decoding procedure in the method was replaced, so rule 6 selects ALGORITHM.

The bug diff reduces time_difference to "total_seconds(self.time - track_point.time)", removing the ordering that subtracted the earlier time from the later one, so the result is signed and goes negative when the argument precedes self, as the specification demonstrates. The reference repair restores the magnitude computation. The None guard is merely reordered and equivalent, so the correction is the value the function computes.

The bug diff rewrites Optional.__init__ so that self.key is set to the raw schema object and is assigned unconditionally, where the working code set "self.key = str(self._schema)" only when a default was supplied; the key that dictionary validation matches against when filling in defaults is therefore wrong, which is the missing-default behaviour in the specification and both failing tests. The reference repair restores that assignment. The same edit drops the TypeError guard on non-comparable schemas, which makes CHECKING arguable, so rule 4 decides.

The bug diff inserts an extra validation into the TupleExpr lvalue branch that reports "can't assign to ()" whenever the tuple has no items, so an empty-tuple target emits a spurious diagnostic ahead of the iterable error that is the correct one. The reference repair deletes that condition and leaves the analyze_tuple_or_list_lvalue call as the only action. The correction is removing an incorrect validation condition.

The bug diff changes how Worksheet.batch_update calls the client: the render and input options are split out into a separate "params" argument and the request body is reduced to just the data list, where the working code passed a single body carrying valueInputOption, includeValuesInResponse and the render options alongside the data. The reference repair restores the original body and the single-argument call. The specification reports a TypeError from this call, so the correction is the argument contract with the values_batch_update API.

The bug diff reverses the operands of two "%" formatting expressions, so the message and its argument are swapped when raising FileNotFoundError and the bad-error-data exception, and it changes the fd-closing pairing from "zip([2] + spass_fds, spass_fds + [max_fd])" to "[max_fd] + spass_fds", which makes closerange span the wrong intervals and closes descriptors that were meant to be passed through. The reference repair restores all three expressions. Each correction is a local implementation fix to an expression, with no guard, binding or component boundary involved.

The bug diff replaces the loop in _get_css_classes that walks a token type up to its nearest STANDARD_TYPES ancestor, prepending each ancestor's class, with a single-level lookup, so a custom type such as Name.Blubb yields only its own class instead of the "n n-Blubb" hierarchy the specification expects. The reference repair restores the ancestor walk. The correction is the traversal inside one method, with no guard, binding or boundary change.

The bug diff hoists the fallback "return None, additional_prefix, 0" to the first line of _close_fstring_if_necessary, making the loop that scans fstring_stack for a node to close unreachable, so the tokenizer never closes an f-string. Every name it returns is a parameter, so nothing is unbound; what is lost is the search itself. The reference repair moves the fallback back below the loop, which is a control-flow correction inside one function.

The bug diff strips the state updates out of _path_to_elements while leaving every branch condition intact: the "path = path[4:]" trim and the brackets and inside_quotes initializations are gone, the inside_quotes toggle and the "elem = ''" resets are removed, three "elem += char" accumulations become pass, and "prev_char = char" is dropped. The reference repair restores each of them. The breadth of a broken parser makes ALGORITHM arguable, but every removed statement is an assignment or initialization and the control flow is untouched, so rule 4 selects ASSIGNMENT.

The bug diff rewrites X509Extension.__str__ so the rendered text is prefixed with "critical," whenever get_critical() is true, which is why str() of a critical basicConstraints extension no longer equals "CA:FALSE" as the specification expects; it also replaces the _openssl_assert on X509V3_EXT_print with a placeholder string. The reference repair restores the original text production and the assertion. The dropped assert makes CHECKING arguable, but what the failing test exercises is the representation the method builds, so rule 6 selects ALGORITHM.

The bug diff hoists "return self._apply(var_func, name='var', numeric_only=numeric_only)" to the first statement of ExponentialMovingWindow.var, above the times check, the window_func setup and the def that binds var_func, so the name is unbound when the return evaluates it and the rest of the method is unreachable. The reference repair moves the return back to the end. Treating the reordering as control flow makes ALGORITHM arguable, but the operative correction is binding var_func before it is used, so rule 4 selects ASSIGNMENT.

The bug diff swaps the two returns of the Finnish business-id check digit while leaving the "sum_ % 11 == 0" test unchanged, so a zero remainder yields str(11 - 0) and every other remainder yields "0", inverting the checksum rule. The reference repair swaps them back. Because the swapped values are returned rather than assigned, rule 4 does not apply and the correction is to the check-digit computation, so rule 6 selects ALGORITHM; a reviewer reading the returned constants as values would find ASSIGNMENT plausible.

The bug diff deletes the "if len(chunk_size) == 0: raise InvalidChunkSize(chunk_size)" validation from ChunkedReader, so an empty chunk-size field passes the hex-digit test vacuously and reaches int(chunk_size, 16). The reference repair restores exactly that check and nothing else. Both failing cases are malformed chunked requests, so the correction is validation of the input before use.

The bug diff deletes IoTDataPlaneResponse.setup_class, whose only purpose was to call the base class with use_raw_body=True; without it the request body is handled with the base default and a non-UTF-8 payload raises UnicodeDecodeError as the specification shows. The reference repair restores the override verbatim. The correction is the argument this handler passes across the boundary to its base class rather than any computation of its own.

The bug diff removes the single line that rebinds verify from config.get("tools.files.download:verify", default=verify), while the neighbouring retry and retry_wait config lookups are left in place, so the configured SSL verification setting never reaches the downloader. The reference repair restores that one assignment. The correction is a missing value assignment, which is exactly what the verify-conf test exercises.

The bug diff strips most of validate_access_token_request: the transport-security and mandatory parameter checks, the missing resource owner and missing verifier guards, the check_request_token format test, the timestamp and nonce validation, and the validate_client_key and validate_request_token calls with their dummy-credential fallbacks. Only the verifier format test survives, and the docstring is left as a stray expression mid-body. The reference repair restores the validation sequence, and the failing tests name the individual checks, so the correction is validation logic.

The bug diff reduces duration_isoformat to a bare "return strftime(tduration, format)", discarding the sign determination that prefixed "-" when a Duration has negative years, months or tdelta, or when a timedelta is negative. Negative durations therefore format without their sign, which is what the specification and the failing negative-duration cases show. The reference repair restores the block. The restored code assigns ret from a condition, so ASSIGNMENT and CHECKING are arguable, but the missing piece is a term of the formatted result, so rule 6 selects ALGORITHM.

The bug diff rewrites the file-type dispatch in get_dependencies to test FileType.VIRTUAL_ENV, FileType.REQUIREMENTS and FileType.PYTHON instead of VIRTUAL_ENVIRONMENT, REQUIREMENTS_TXT, POETRY_LOCK, PIPENV_LOCK and PYPROJECT_TOML, and drops the "if not f.file_type" early return, so no supported manifest is recognised and scans come back empty. The reference repair restores the original conditions and grouping. Because the names tested belong to another module's FileType enum, INTERFACE is arguable, but no signature or protocol changed and the correction is the dispatch condition set inside one function, so rule 5 selects CHECKING.

The bug diff moves "message_bytes = data[start:end]" to the end of MultiPartParser.on_part_data, below the size check, the data.extend call and the file-part append that all read it, leaving the name unbound at every use. The reference repair puts the binding back at the top of the method. The correction is the placement of one local initialization, and every multipart parsing test depends on it.

The bug diff replaces the NUMERIC_VALIDATOR_LOOKUP table exported by _validators.py with a private _CONSTRAINT_TO_VALIDATOR_LOOKUP plus a get_constraint_validator accessor, drops the Decimal import and the decimal digit validators, and rewrites _known_annotated_metadata.py to import the new accessor and call add_js_update_schema and NUMERIC_CONSTRAINTS in place of the inline metadata update. The whole suite then fails at collection, as the specification reports. The reference repair restores the exported table, the decimal validators and the original consumer code. The removed decimal validators make FUNCTION arguable, but the correction is the names one module exports and the other imports, so rule 3 selects INTERFACE.

The bug diff removes the trailing step of the slice builder, which appended slice(source_idx, len(raw_source_string)) whenever the last patch ended before the end of the source, so the returned buffer no longer covers the tail of the file. The reference repair restores that step. The restored code is introduced by a bounds comparison, which makes CHECKING arguable, but it completes the slice enumeration rather than validating anything, so rule 6 selects ALGORITHM.

The bug diff deletes the whole keyword-matching loop from the tokenizer's keyword scan: the trie walk over in_trie, the recording of word on TrieResult.EXISTS, the character accumulation with whitespace collapsing, and the size and single_token bookkeeping. Nothing remains to identify a keyword before the "if word" branch. The reference repair restores the loop unchanged. The correction is a local traversal over the keyword trie, with no guard, binding or interface change involved.

The bug diff rewrites Scope.scope_ref_count to tally over scope.sources rather than scope.selected_sources, seeds unreferenced scopes with explicit zeros, and returns a plain dict instead of the defaultdict callers rely on, so reference counts no longer reflect how often a CTE is actually selected and eliminate_ctes stops inlining. The reference repair restores the original tally. The specification names the sources versus selected_sources swap, and the correction is the counting logic inside one method.

The bug diff replaces PDFStructElement.to_dict's asdict serialization and breadth-first prune over the whole element tree with a hand-built dict holding only children plus optional role_map and class_map, pruned at the top level only. Every other field is dropped and nested elements keep their empty values, which is the missing and incorrect attribute behaviour the specification describes. The reference repair restores the asdict call and the deque-driven traversal. The correction is the serialization and traversal inside one method.

The bug diff removes the loop in _resolve_refs_in_parameter_or_header that walked each media type under a parameter's "content" and called _resolve_schema on it, so a schema named inside parameter content is left as a bare string instead of becoming a $ref, exactly as the specification shows. The reference repair restores the three lines. The correction is a missing descent step in the reference-resolution traversal.

The bug diff drops the default_kwargs dict and passes read_only, data_only and keep_links to openpyxl's load_workbook as fixed keyword arguments with **engine_kwargs splatted alongside, so a user value for any of those three can no longer take effect. The reference repair restores the "default_kwargs | engine_kwargs" merge that gives caller-supplied kwargs precedence. Reading the merge as a value computation makes ASSIGNMENT or ALGORITHM arguable, but the defect is which parameters reach the external library call, so rule 3 selects INTERFACE.

The bug diff moves "rels_of_reltype = self._rels_by_reltype[reltype]" to the last line of part_with_reltype, below the return, so the name is unbound at the two length checks and at the return itself; the docstring is also displaced into the body and the two guards swapped, though those guards are mutually exclusive so their order is immaterial. The reference repair puts the binding back above its uses. The correction is the placement of one local initialization.

The bug diff strips imported names across the EC2 modules while leaving their uses in place: TypeVar is dropped from the typing import in utils.py, Optional from hosts.py, the typing imports from fleets.py and flow_logs.py, and SpotInstanceRequest from the spot_requests import in fleets.py. Loading the package then raises the "name 'TypeVar' is not defined" NameError the specification quotes. The reference repair restores each import and the annotations that use them. Reading the imports as missing module-level bindings makes ASSIGNMENT arguable, but the correction is what these modules import from others, so rule 3 selects INTERFACE.

The bug diff restructures _container_getitem and loses the "except ValueError" arm that wrapped the subscript operation and re-raised it as AstroidValueError, keeping only an IndexError arm for constant indices and an AstroidTypeError arm around _infer_slice. A zero-step slice therefore lets the interpreter's ValueError escape, which is the single failing test and the behaviour the specification describes. The reference repair restores the ValueError, IndexError and TypeError handlers. The wider rewrite of node construction makes ALGORITHM arguable, but only the exception handling changes observable behaviour, so rule 5 selects CHECKING.

The bug diff attaches the generated help text to new_func instead of to the returned decorator and changes both the default doc_description and the sentence template, so pass_meta_key's decorator carries no such __doc__; it also replaces ctx.invoke(f, obj, ...) with a direct call. The reference repair restores the assignment to decorator.__doc__ with the original text and the ctx.invoke call. Rule 8 was considered but the defective artifact is the code that sets the attribute, not a documentation file, and rule 3 does not dominate because the invoke change is not what the failing test exercises; the correction is an attribute assigned on the wrong object with the wrong value, so rule 4 selects ASSIGNMENT.

The bug diff deletes every parameter check from date_of_birth: the integer type tests for minimum_age and maximum_age, the two non-negative range checks, and the minimum_age <= maximum_age ordering check. The reference repair restores all five. The same edit also rewrites the date range computation, which makes ALGORITHM arguable, but the specification and the single failing test_value_errors case are entirely about the missing ValueErrors, so rule 5 selects CHECKING.

The bug diff drops the "or not os.path.exists(frame.f_code.co_filename)" clause from the frame walk in find_dotenv, so frames whose reported filename has no counterpart on disk, as with modules imported from a zip archive, are no longer skipped and the search starts from a path that does not exist. The reference repair restores that clause. Because the weakened predicate is a loop condition, ALGORITHM is arguable, but the missing clause is an existence test on a value before it is used, so rule 5 selects CHECKING.
